tasks.brief:
Implementation constraints: Edit `src/services/storage.py`. Add module-level `threading.Lock()` for atomic read-modify-write. Define `class SnapshotConflict(Exception):` with attribute `current_revision`. Implement `load_versioned_snapshot() -> tuple[list[dict], int]` and `save_versioned_snapshot(threads, expected_revision) -> int`. Keep existing `load_snapshot` and `save_snapshot` as compatibility wrappers (save_snapshot must acquire the same lock and advance generation). Replace the `except OSError: pass` at the temp-cleanup block (approx line 79) with `logging.warning(...)` including the temp path and exception, then re-raise the original save failure.

Behavioral specification: `load_versioned_snapshot` reads the primary JSON file. If missing, returns `([], 0)`. If it is a raw list (legacy), returns `(list, 0)`. If it is an object with `revision` and `threads`, returns `(threads, revision)`. `save_versioned_snapshot` acquires the lock, loads the current state via the same logic, compares the loaded revision to `expected_revision`. On mismatch, raises `SnapshotConflict(current_revision=loaded_revision)` before writing anything. On match, writes a temp file with `{"revision": loaded_revision + 1, "threads": threads}`, atomically replaces the primary, rotates the old primary to `.bak` (only one `.bak` kept), and returns the new revision. If the current on-disk form was legacy (raw list), the write migrates it to the revision envelope (revision 1). `save_snapshot` acquires the lock, loads current revision, and calls `save_versioned_snapshot(threads, current_revision)`.

Acceptance condition: `load_versioned_snapshot` and `save_versioned_snapshot` are defined. `SnapshotConflict` is defined with `current_revision`. The temp-cleanup block logs a warning instead of silently passing. Legacy raw-list files are read at revision 0 and migrated to revision 1 on next write.

Implementation constraints: Edit `src/api/threads.py`. Import `SnapshotConflict` from `src.services.storage`. Extend `ThreadsPayload` with required `revision: int >= 0`. Add a DELETE body model (e.g. `ThreadsRevisionPrecondition`) with required `revision: int >= 0`. Use `route:GET /api/v1/threads`, `route:PUT /api/v1/threads`, `route:DELETE /api/v1/threads`. Map `SnapshotConflict` to HTTP 409 with body `{"error":"revision_conflict", "current_revision": n}` using `JSONResponse`, not FastAPI's default `detail` wrapper.

Behavioral specification: GET `/api/v1/threads` calls `load_versioned_snapshot()`, returns `{"threads": [...], "revision": n, "quarantined": bool}` (quarantined logic from existing code). PUT `/api/v1/threads` validates `ThreadsPayload` (revision required), calls `save_versioned_snapshot(payload.threads, payload.revision)`, returns `{"status":"ok", "revision": new_revision}`. DELETE `/api/v1/threads` validates the revision body model, calls `save_versioned_snapshot([], body.revision)`, returns `{"status":"ok", "revision": new_revision}`. Validation failures (missing revision) return 422 and write nothing. `SnapshotConflict` raises 409 with the specified JSON body.

Acceptance condition: GET returns threads, revision, and quarantined flag. PUT and DELETE require revision in body, return new revision. Missing revision returns 422. Stale revision returns 409 with `current_revision`. Validation errors do not modify the snapshot file.

Implementation constraints: Edit `src/static/threads.js`. Add state variables: `_revision` (hydrated from GET), `_pendingSnapshots` (queue of thread arrays), `_isPersisting` (boolean), `_conflictLatched` (boolean). Add `setRevision(n)` method. Add `_enqueueSave(threads)` and `_flushQueue()` methods. Use `fetch` for PUT/DELETE. Do not coalesce snapshots; each mutation enqueues its own snapshot.

Behavioral specification: `setRevision(n)` sets `_revision = n` and clears `_conflictLatched` and `save-status`. `_enqueueSave(threads)` pushes `threads` to `_pendingSnapshots`; if not `_isPersisting` and not `_conflictLatched`, calls `_flushQueue()`. `_flushQueue()` pops the first snapshot, sets `_isPersisting = true`, issues PUT `/api/v1/threads` with body `{threads: snapshot, revision: _revision}`. On 200, parses response `revision`, sets `_revision = response.revision`, clears `save-status`, and if queue is non-empty, recursively calls `_flushQueue()`; else sets `_isPersisting = false`. On 409, sets `_conflictLatched = true`, clears `_pendingSnapshots`, sets `_isPersisting = false`, writes `history changed elsewhere — reload required` to `el('save-status').textContent`. On other errors, writes `not saved` to `save-status`, sets `_isPersisting = false` (does not retry or clear queue on transient error per AC-75/76). Existing mutation functions (createThread, deleteThread, updateTitle, etc.) must be updated to call `_enqueueSave(ThreadSnapshotList)` instead of direct PUT. `restoreThreadModelState` and `lockThread` edits from prior delta remain (no model-select disable).

Acceptance condition: `_enqueueSave` queues snapshots. `_flushQueue` serializes them with revision bumping. 409 latches the page and shows the conflict message. Non-409 errors show `not saved`. `setRevision` is exposed for app.js to call during hydration.

Implementation constraints: Edit `src/static/app.js`. During startup hydration (the initial GET `/api/v1/threads`), extract `data.revision` and call `Threads.setRevision(data.revision)` before rendering or creating state. Ensure `save-status` is empty and the conflict latch is cleared on reload. If GET returns empty threads, the default-thread creation (existing behavior) will enqueue a save against the returned revision.

Behavioral specification: In the startup sequence, after the GET `/api/v1/threads` response arrives, set `Threads` revision via the exposed hook. Do not infer revision from content. A healthy reload starts with empty `save-status` and an unlatched state. The existing default-thread creation flow (when no threads exist) must enqueue its save via `Threads._enqueueSave` so it uses the hydrated revision.

Acceptance condition: On page load, the revision from the GET response is installed in the Threads persistence owner. The save-status element is empty. The conflict latch is cleared. Default thread creation enqueues a save with the correct initial revision.
